messages:
aisha_cs: Heads-up — Neptune Analytics reported increased tail latency after their private deployment cutover last night. p95 spiked to ~380ms between ~02:10–03:40 UTC. Need to align on SLO impact + credit calc before renewal chat. @miguel_ops can you pull the latency/error slice and incident window?

miguel_ops: On it. grabbing traces and pod metrics now. initial glance shows KV cache misses during warmup and some retry storms. will post a short TL;DR and the exact window in a minute.

raj_sales: Putting this on radar for renewal — Neptune's CSM flagged performance as the top concern last week. if we owe credits it affects the deal math. can we confirm whether this violates their 99.95% monthly uptime SLO?

hannah_neptune: Confirming from our side — we saw customer-facing latencies and a couple timed-out requests in the ingestion endpoint. Impacted 3/12 tenants, reduced throughput for ~90 minutes. We're collecting logs for our support case. appreciate fast clarity on credits.

miguel_ops: TL;DR: incident window 2023-11-12 02:08–03:40 UTC (92m). platform telemetry: overall host availability unaffected, but request p95 for model-infer route jumped to 380ms -> normal ~110ms. root cause: cache population + a misconfigured autoscaling cooldown that prevented pod spin-up. attaching quick snippet from alert history: 

```
[02:08] alert: p95_infer > 300ms (neptune-prod)
[02:20] autoscaler failed to scale due to cooldown
[03:00] cache warmed, p95 trending down
[03:40] p95 back to normal
```

miguel_ops: Based on logs error-rate stayed <0.5% but latency breach lasted ~92 minutes. will ask infra to whitelist this autoscaler tweak for their cluster to avoid recurrence.

aisha_cs: Quick question — Neptune is on a reserved capacity plan with monthly uptime SLA 99.95% and explicit credit formula in appendix B. Does 92 minutes translate to a credit? we need a suggested credit amount and proposed customer email, plus an enablement session to show hardening steps.

raj_sales: Appendix B states: credit = prorated percentage of monthly fee based on downtime beyond SLA. Example calc: `credit_pct = (downtime_minutes - allowed_minutes)/total_minutes_in_month`. For 99.95% SLA allowed monthly downtime ≈ 21.6 minutes. so breach = 92 - 21.6 = 70.4 minutes.

raj_sales: If their monthly reserved fee is $18,000: `credit = (70.4 / 43200) * 18000 ≈ $29.3` — rounding rules in contract say round to nearest $10, so ~$30 credit.

hannah_neptune: That number seems small given customer impact — is there discretion to offer a goodwill credit or extended support instead? they raised concerns about reliability in renewal feedback.

aisha_cs: Good point. propose: offer the contractual credit (~$30) but add a one-time goodwill credit of $1,500 + a joint enablement + runbook review (30m) and a post-migration health check in 2 weeks. that should mitigate renewal risk.

miguel_ops: I support. I'll push the autoscaler cooldown change and add a safeguard: pre-warm cache on deploys for Neptune's routes and a brief runbook update. will share the ops PR link once created.

deploy-bot: deploy event: ops/pr/842 merged by miguel_ops — "neptune: autoscaler cooldown fix + cache prewarm" (sha: a1b2c3)

aisha_cs: Action items: 1) raj to draft customer email with credit + goodwill offer (due EOD), 2) miguel to link PR + ops runbook update, 3) schedule 30m enablement with Neptune (prefer Tue or Wed next week) — i put a tentative :calendar: invite. I'll loop in legal for the credit wording.

raj_sales: Drafted email ready for review, posting in thread shortly.

hannah_neptune: Thanks team — appreciate the transparency. We'll review the invite and confirm time.

aisha_cs: Closing note — capturing feedback for product: add an SLO heatmap per-tenant in Console + optional stronger alerts for reserved customers. filing a product request now. :white_check_mark:
